title: Prithvi Sukta | Atharvaveda, Earth is my mother
desc: Atharvaveda 12.1.12, Prithvi Sukta: the mantra in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how it is used.
caption: Atharvaveda 12.1.12, Prithvi Sukta
intro: This is a mantra from the **Atharvaveda** (Atharvaveda 12.1.12, Prithvi Sukta). Below are the Sanskrit text and a **plain English meaning**.
takeaways: The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda.
Vedic mantras are learned by listening and repeating.

p: **यत्ते मध्यं पृथिवि यच्च नभ्यं यास्त ऊर्जस्तन्वः संबभूवुः । तासु नो धेह्यभि नः पवस्व माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः । पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु ॥**
Earth, set us among the forces that rise from your centre and navel. Earth is my mother, I am her son. May Parjanya, the rain, my father, nourish me.
The Atharvaveda is one of the four Vedas, the oldest scriptures of Sanatana Dharma, handed down by voice for thousands of years.

faq.a: Earth, set us among the forces that rise from your centre and navel. Earth is my mother, I am her son. May Parjanya, the rain, my father, nourish me.
There are **four**: Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering.
